facts.text: The word 'heart' (qalb) in Arabic comes from the root q-l-b, meaning 'to turn' — because the heart constantly turns between states. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) said: 'The heart is called qalb because it turns over in every state.'

Mulla Sadra's Asfar (The Four Journeys) was so revolutionary that contemporary scholars declared it heresy. He was exiled from Shiraz and took refuge in the village of Kahak near Qom — where he wrote his most profound works.
Shaykh Bahai (Shaykh Baha'i) was both a grand Shi'a jurist and a master of mathematics, astronomy, and esoteric sciences. He wrote on astrology and the secrets of letters — and saw no contradiction.
Ibn Arabi wrote over 500 works. When asked about the shortest path to knowledge of God, he replied: 'Know yourself.' When asked for something shorter, he said: 'Be silent.'
Surah al-Fatiha contains exactly seven verses — matching the seven heavens, the seven earths, and the seven circumambulations of the Kaaba. Every recitation is a cosmic ascent.

The Prophet Muhammad (SAW) said: 'Whoever recites Qul Huwa Allahu Ahad (Surah al-Ikhlas) ten times, Allah builds for him a palace in Paradise.' This single surah contains one-third of the Quran in meaning.
Imam Ali (AS) used to pray 1000 rakats of nafilah prayer every day and night. His son Imam al-Hasan (AS) said: 'I never saw my father tire of worship — his soul found rest in it.'
The angel Jibra'il (AS) did not enter the house of Sayyida Fatima (AS) for three days after the Prophet's (SAW) death — because the light had left that home. It is said he wept.

The phrase 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim' contains 19 Arabic letters. The keepers of Hell (Zabaniyah) are also 19. Imam Ali (AS) said: 'Bismillah is the key to every closed door; recite it and the gates of mercy open.'
Ayn al-Qudat Hamadani wrote Tamhidat at age 28 — a masterpiece of Sufi metaphysics. He was executed at 33 for his views. His last words were: 'The wine of love was too strong for this world.'
Shaykh al-Ra'is Ibn Sina read Aristotle's Metaphysics 40 times without understanding it — until al-Farabi's commentary made it click. He wrote a note of thanks in the margin.
In Islamic eschatology, Imam al-Mahdi (AJ) will emerge on the Day of Ashura — the same day Imam Husayn (AS) was martyred. The day that began in tragedy will end in justice.
The Kaaba has been rebuilt at least 12 times in history. Imam Ali (AS) was born inside the Kaaba — the only person in history honored with birth in the House of Allah.
Mulla Husayn Quli Hamadani said: 'The journey to Allah is not measured in miles but in breaths. Each breath can take you closer or farther — there is no standing still.'
Jabir ibn Hayyan, the father of chemistry, was a student of Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS). The Imam taught him alchemy, astronomy, and the science of the soul — knowledge above and below.

wit.text: A mureed asked his Pir: 'Master, how long have I been in your company?' The Pir replied: 'Son, you haven't even asked when you arrived. If the question hasn't arisen, how can the answer come?'
A man asked Ibn Arabi: 'How do I know God?' Ibn Arabi said: 'Do you know who is asking?' The man said: 'I am.' Ibn Arabi said: 'Then you already know.'
Mulla Nasruddin was asked: 'What happens after death?' The Mulla said: 'Forget about after death — first see what this life before death is, then ask.'
A student asked Allamah Tabatabai: 'How did you write such a massive tafsir?' The Allamah smiled: 'You read each verse — I asked each verse.'
Shaykh Ansari was asked: 'What is the most difficult ruling in fiqh?' He thought and said: 'To stop yourself from giving your own opinion when the truth has already been spoken.'

Imam al-Ghazali was asked: 'You mastered the outward sciences — why did you then abandon them for the path of the heart?' Ghazali said: 'The outward told me where the door was; the inward let me enter.'

A man went to a sage and said: 'I want to see God.' The sage replied: 'Close your eyes and look inward.' The man closed his eyes and said: 'I see nothing.' The sage said: 'Then you looked with eyes — not with the heart.'

Shaykh Baha'i dreamt of Imam al-Zaman (AJ) and asked: 'Master, what is the shortest path?' The Imam replied: 'Wait — you're still asking about paths? Start walking and the path will rise beneath your feet.'
A philosopher asked Rumi: 'You speak of love — but what is its proof?' Rumi replied: 'The proof of fire is that it burns. Come closer.'
A faqih was explaining the proofs of God's existence. A simple man interrupted: 'Sir, you speak as if He is lost and needs to be found. I speak as if He is here and needs to be felt.'
Mulla Nasruddin saw a group arguing about the essence of God. He laughed and said: 'You remind me of blind men describing an elephant — each touching a different part, each sure he alone is right.'
